text:
maya (support): FYI customer reported a big QPS drop on their Dedicated pool this morning, started ~08:10 PT. ticket #C-4821. They see 200->30 qps and lots of 429/stream timeouts.
alex (eng-runtime): can you paste customer pool id + sample request IDs?
maya (support): pool=dedicated-rw-57, example req ids: req_8a2, req_8b1, req_8f3. customer says latency spiked 200ms->2s before 429s.
jamie (oncall): I pulled first-pass metrics: steady arrival rate, but effective throughput collapsed. queue_time p50 jumped from 30ms to 700ms. CPU/GPU look fine.
lina (runtime): that pattern smells like many tiny packs making kernel launch overhead dominate. any recent scheduler/pack config flips?
alex (eng-runtime): ops rolled out a tweak last night to reduce "max_pack_tokens" to 64 for that tenant (to improve latency for short requests). might be oversharing the pack window across busy clients.
maya (support): customer insists they didn't change anything on their side. billing shows normal usage.
jamie (oncall): can we repro with a synthetic load that mirrors their traffic? low token requests but high request-per-second. I'll spin a quick script.
alex (eng-runtime): pls include the X-Redwood-Pool header to ensure requests land on ded-rw-57. use concurrency 80 and payload length ~12 tokens.
jamie (oncall): posting repro here:
```bash
# simulate many short requests to dedicated-rw-57
for i in {1..1000}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
    -H 'X-Redwood-Pool: dedicated-rw-57' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"tiny-chat-1","input":"hi","max_tokens":12}' &
  if (( i % 80 == 0 )); then wait; fi
done
```
jamie (oncall): repro logs: many requests returned 200 but per-token throughput stalled; a subset saw 429s with reason "pack_capacity_exceeded".
alex (eng-runtime): that error is from the packer when aggregated token budget for a window exceeds pool token cap. lowering max_pack_tokens reduces aggregation and increases per-request overhead — exactly what we're seeing.
lina (runtime): checking scheduler history: change was deployed 02:10 UTC last night for "latency experiment" and targeted a wide set of tenants including this pool. it seems to backfire for high-rps short-context workloads.
maya (support): customer is pushing back hard; they want immediate mitigation.
alex (eng-runtime): short-term mitigation: revert max_pack_tokens for dedicated-rw-57 to 256 and reopen the pack window to allow larger aggregates. also enable adaptive_pack=true. That should reduce kernel overhead and restore throughput.
jamie (oncall): I'm going to create a temporary route rule to direct this customer's traffic to backup pool ded-backup-12 while we roll the config. creating change now.
(ticket-bot): ticket#C-4821 updated: temporary routing applied -> ded-backup-12.
maya (support): customer confirms traffic moved and latency improved to ~220ms, qps back to ~190. they still saw a few residual 429s.
alex (eng-runtime): residual 429s expected while caches warm. I'll push config revert:
```json
{"selector":"pool:dedicated-rw-57","max_pack_tokens":256,"adaptive_pack":true}
```
alex (eng-runtime): applied. monitoring; also adding a short-term autoscale bump (+2 GPUs) to absorb initial surge while packer warms.
lina (runtime): noted — we should investigate canary logic for pack config changes. experiment targeted too broadly.
jamie (oncall): logs after revert show queue_time p50 back to ~40ms, p95 300ms. no new pack_capacity errors.
maya (support): customer is happy for now, asked for postmortem and assurance it won't recur.
alex (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) roll back global tweak and create a targeted canary for homogeneous workloads, 2) add a coverage test that simulates high-rps short-token workloads to catch regressions, 3) run a one-hour soak on ded pools after future pack changes. I'll own the follow-ups.
lina (runtime): assigning follow-up ticket INF-789 to alex.
maya (support): thanks all — I'll update the customer and close the urgent escalation once INF-789 is tracked. :tada:
alex (eng-runtime): filing a short postmortem summary after the metrics stabilize, will ping here.
jamie (oncall): leaving notes for SRE runbook: consider auto-revert threshold when pack_capacity_exceeded > 0.5% for 5m.
maya (support): closing loop — customer says billing unaffected, no auth issues. they appreciated the quick mitigation.
alex (eng-runtime): good catch, everyone.
